hypothesis: Accepted extant species of shelled molluscs, cephalopods and crustaceans are exceptional in fresh water and are present in brackish water.
pass_criterion: Supports only if all three groups pass. A group passes when, among accepted extant species with any aquatic flag, the fraction that are fresh and not marine is below 0.05, and at least one species is flagged brackish. Groups: testaceans = Mollusca excluding Cephalopoda; cephalopods = Cephalopoda; crustaceans = Crustacea.
fail_criterion: A group refutes when that fresh-and-not-marine fraction is at least 0.15. The claim refutes if at least two groups refute. Mixed if exactly one group refutes and at least one group passes. Inconclusive, reason data-unavailable or underpowered, otherwise (crawl incomplete, or no group refutes and not all groups pass). Species with no marine, brackish or freshwater flag are left out of the denominator. Terrestrial-only species are not counted as freshwater.

test_contract.expected_observation: For shelled molluscs, cephalopods and crustaceans, fewer than 5 percent of aquatic accepted extant species are fresh and not marine, and brackish species are recorded in each group.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: In a group, at least 15 percent of aquatic accepted extant species are fresh and not marine.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: World Register of Marine Species Aphia records with isMarine, isBrackish and isFreshwater flags, accepted species rank, extant. WoRMS catalogues non-marine taxa when marine_only is off. Testaceans are Mollusca other than Cephalopoda, because cephalopods are named separately in the claim.
test_contract.inference_method: Count accepted extant species by environment flag from the WoRMS REST API. Fresh-and-not-marine fraction = species with isFreshwater true and isMarine not true, divided by species with any of the three aquatic flags. Below 0.05 and brackish count at least 1 passes a group; at least 0.15 refutes a group. Two refuted groups refute the claim; one refuted and one passed is mixed.

interpretation: Bloodless aquatic animals in the quote are testaceans, cephalopods and crustaceans. 'Not found in lakes or the fresher brackish waters, except exceptionally' is read as a fresh-and-not-marine share under 5 percent of aquatic species. Fifteen percent or more is not exceptional. 'Estuaries and river mouths' requires the brackish flag to be used at least once. Terrestrial snails are outside this claim.

deviations.change: Species-rank lists longer than 20,000 rows were probed at exponentially increasing offsets and not fully downloaded.
deviations.why: Mollusca still returned a full page at offset 200001-scale and Crustacea did too past 100,000 rows. Completing those crawls was not possible in this run. The pass and fail fractions were not changed. The pre-registered rule says an incomplete crawl is inconclusive.

method: WoRMS Aphia IDs for Mollusca, Crustacea and Cephalopoda were resolved, then species-rank pages were requested with marine_only false. The length of each list was probed by quadrupling the offset until a short page or until the list passed 20,000 rows. Only lists within that bound were fully downloaded. Accepted extant species were tallied by isMarine, isBrackish and isFreshwater. Cephalopoda was fully counted. Mollusca and Crustacea were not, so the three-group test is incomplete and the verdict is inconclusive.

measured.unit: cephalopod fresh-and-not-marine fraction among aquatic accepted species

caveats: The cephalopod fraction is a finished count and is reported, but it does not decide the claim by itself.
Unaccepted names and synonyms are in the species-rank pages and were excluded from the tally.
extant_only was requested; records with isExtinct equal to 1 were also dropped.
Terrestrial-only species are outside the aquatic denominator, as pre-registered.

datasets.name: WoRMS Aphia species-rank records with environment flags

files.role: manifest of fully downloaded cephalopod pages

headline: WoRMS species-rank lists for molluscs and crustaceans still fill a page past 20,000 rows, so the three-group test is unfinished; of 869 accepted extant aquatic cephalopod species, 0 are fresh and not marine (fraction 0.0) and 1 is brackish.
